clue.text: Concentrate on the film?

parts.note: a camera operator sharpening the image so the picture on the film is crisp; also simply to pay close attention

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an order to watch a movie closely, but it also describes adjusting a camera so the picture is sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate is to fix attention; a lens setting gives a sharp image on film, the same word in photography.

clue.text: Hester's other name

indicators.note: an other version of the word Hester means its letters made into a different arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone asks what alternative name a woman called Hester goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges HESTER; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, the biblical queen of Persia.

clue.text: Shipping company taking flowers

parts.note: the reading of a florists' freight firm hides small vessels that trade along a coastline, where flowers are rivers, things that flow

explanation.walkthrough: Crossword 'flowers' are often rivers (things that flow); these vessels ply coasts and estuaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cargo ships working the shoreline trade carry a fleet's worth of craft on routes past river mouths.

clue.text: Coach begins to fill a gap in niece's muddled knowledge

indicators.note: one piece slots into a space within another, so it goes inside
muddled letters are mixed up, so these are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word niece's, apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: the beginning of the word coach, its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A tutor tries to patch the holes in a confused young relative's learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges NIECES into SIENCE, and 'to fill a gap in' puts C (Coach begins) in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Systematic learning about the world; the Latin root scientia simply means learning.

clue.text: Act when some came in late

indicators.note: one piece entering another sits inside it

parts.note: an act is a deed
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: A theatrical scene runs during which certain latecomers took their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came in' puts PART inside DEED. 'Act' and 'came in' pull towards a stage, but 'late' means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the sense of recently dead, a euphemism also used of the deceased.

clue.text: Its contents are usually back to front

definitions.text: Its contents are usually back to front

parts.words: Its contents are usually back to front
parts.note: volumes stand with their spines, their backs, facing outward toward the room

explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' sounds like a mistake, but books on a shelf show their backs (spines) to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture holding volumes upright, the spine of each facing out to the reader.

clue.text: Jump to end the game

parts.note: a small jump is a hop
to scotch a plan is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: Someone leaps up to call a halt to the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground pastime of jumping through chalked squares.

clue.text: The way to live down under

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: Advice on how to settle in Australia, the land down under.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower than something, beneath it.

clue.text: Effrontery, more than cheek

definitions.meaning: boldness, as in having the nerve to do something
the whole front of the head, of which a cheek is only part

explanation.definitionFit: Effrontery as in brazen nerve; and the front of the head, which takes in the cheeks and more.

clue.text: Way to serve potatoes, just stuffed with game

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with another holds it inside

parts.note: just, as in deserved, is due
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Fair enough that the spuds come filled with venison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like venison stuffing; it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of piped, egg-enriched mashed potato, browned in the oven.

clue.text: Nearest thing to the old USSR in the US

definitions.text: Nearest thing to the old USSR in the US

parts.words: Nearest thing to the old USSR in the US
parts.note: the American state lying closest geographically to Soviet territory across the Bering Strait, and once Russian itself

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a political jibe about some American institution, but it is literal geography.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state across the Bering Strait from Siberia, bought from Russia in 1867.

clue.text: Release-without charge

explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone; and gratis, costing nothing.

clue.text: Animals involved in the chase

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Creatures taking part in a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Big spotted cats, the fastest land mammals.

clue.text: Ballet posture of Lincoln in square dance

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another goes inside it
to make letters dance is to jumble them

parts.note: Abe is the short name of Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A ballet pose struck by the American president during a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance' rearranges SQUARE to ARSQUE, and 'in' puts ABE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pose on one leg with the other stretched behind, a classical ballet position.

clue.text: My word

parts.note: not an exclamation of surprise but a pledge, as in giving your word

explanation.walkthrough: 'My word!' reads as surprise; read it as 'I give you my word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving your word is a vow or pledge to do something.

clue.text: That many were treated badly was important

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, read as a large number

indicators.note: badly treated letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: It was significant that so many people were handled so poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TREATED to ATTERED; 'That many' stands for M, a thousand in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Counted or signified, carried weight.

clue.text: Key question for the scone-maker

parts.note: G is a musical key
a riddle is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: An important query put to a baker of scones.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat iron plate on which scones and drop scones are baked, a kitchen tool for that baker.

clue.text: Are out in storm, breaking at last

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other
breaking a word apart scatters its letters
out signals the letters of the word are are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Some people are outside in a storm just as it breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns STORM into RMOST, 'out' turns ARE into EAR, and 'in' puts EAR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Last in position, furthest back, as in the hindmost.

clue.text: State crime and motive after trial opens

indicators.note: this piece follows the other in the answer
what opens a word is its first letter

parts.note: a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: A prosecutor names the crime and the motive once the trial begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country, the gravest offence against the state.

clue.text: Place equipped for stock dispatch

parts.note: sounds like a warehouse shipping goods, but stock means livestock and dispatch means kill

explanation.walkthrough: 'stock dispatch' suggests sending goods out from a depot; here it is killing livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse, where farm animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Food of love at first sight

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word sight

explanation.surface: A romantic phrase: the nourishment of love at first sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal grain eaten as porridge and fed to horses.

clue.text: Learner breaks tool making a spindle

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L is a learner, as on an L-plate

explanation.surface: A novice smashes a tool while turning a spindle in the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Officer with a song in his heart-something catchy

indicators.note: the piece goes in the middle of the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A soldier humming a tune with music in his heart, a catchy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something catchy' sounds like a tune, but a lasso catches animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rope with a running noose, used to catch cattle or horses.

clue.text: Reach the heights in music?

definitions.meaning: to climb up to the top of something
a run of notes up or down in order, practised by musicians

explanation.definitionFit: To climb a wall or mountain; and an ordered series of notes such as C major.

clue.text: A hint of a rise

parts.note: a scent is a trace or hint, as a hunting dog follows

explanation.surface: Just a faint suggestion of something going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or upward movement.

clue.text: Is it won by the fastest guns in the West?

definitions.text: Is it won by the fastest guns in the West?

parts.words: Is it won by the fastest guns in the West?
parts.note: sounds like a cowboy shoot-out, but the West here means NATO powers racing for weapons

explanation.walkthrough: 'fastest guns in the West' suggests Wild West gunfighters; read it as Cold War nations stockpiling weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition between states to build up military weapons, as in the Cold War.

clue.text: Is this a drawing instrument found amongst dividers?

definitions.text: Is this a drawing instrument found amongst dividers?

parts.words: Is this a drawing instrument found amongst dividers?
parts.note: a straight-edge kept with compasses and dividers in a geometry set, and also a monarch who divides and rules

explanation.walkthrough: Dividers are a geometry tool, but 'divide and rule' hints at the other sense, a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight-edge for measuring and drawing lines, and a sovereign.

clue.text: He was a painter of some force?

definitions.meaning: the English landscape artist John, of The Hay Wain
a member of a police force

explanation.definitionFit: John, English Romantic landscape artist; and a police officer of the lowest rank.
